title: Server and Browser Differences knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Server and Browser Differences”?
options: Server and Browser Differences should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Server and Browser Differences helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Server and Browser Differences means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Server and Browser Differences removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: Server and Browser Differences helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Server and Browser Differences is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Browser-specific APIs” in this lesson?
options: Connect “Browser-specific APIs” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Browser-specific APIs” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Browser-specific APIs” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Browser-specific APIs” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Browser-specific APIs” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Browser-specific APIs” under Server and Browser Differences. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Server and Browser Differences”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
